sections.overview: This ground-dwelling sandgrouse has a fragmented range across eastern and southern Africa.
sections.identification: The sexes differ in plumage; males show a yellow throat and eyebrow.
sections.habitat: In southern Africa it favors open grassland on fine clay soils and fallow fields.
sections.diet: It feeds on seeds, including seeds of Amaranthus and Crotalaria in one study area.
sections.behavior: Its movements remain poorly understood; southern African birds include residents and arrivals.
sections.reproduction: It nests alone in a shallow, often concealed ground scrape.
sections.ecology: Compare its clay-soil grassland with Namaqua and Spotted Sandgrouse in their linked profiles.
sections.conservation: Global status is Least Concern; South Africa lists it as Near Threatened.
